title: Does my bum look big in this
titleChinese: 我穿牛仔裤看上去是不是屁股很大
paragraphs: "Does my bum look big in this?" That's what I asked myself when I tried on the designer jeans I bought in the Christmas sales and the mirror... well, the mirror didn't actually say anything but I got the message: It's time to go on a diet!

Sometimes we just don't know how many calories we eat. Experts say cooking meals from scratch can help you think about the ingredients which go into your food. Tam Fry, from the UK's National Obesity Forum, says: "Learning how to cook fresh food is really the number one thing to consider when tackling obesity and improving weight loss."

If you can't cook, Fry recommends that you be more aware of what you put in your trolley when you go to the supermarket. He points out: "People don't read food labels. At government level making the labels easier to read and understand is key, but just looking at how many grams of sugar is in something is really important."

Some experts believe that a good way to reduce your waistline might be to start by reducing the size of the plate you eat from. Research has suggested that people eat most of what they serve themselves, so big portions lead to overeating.

A study by Dr Brian Wansink, from Cornell University, US, claimed that reducing plate size from about 30cm to 25cm typically results in 22% fewer calories being served, as the smaller plate makes a normal serving seem more filling. However, once plate size went below about 24cm, "people begin to realise they're tricking themselves and go back for seconds and thirds".

I think I'll keep my current plates for now. As for me, nothing beats an inspiring image on the fridge door - a picture of my lovely jeans - with some wise quote as a caption. As supermodel Kate Moss once said: "Nothing tastes as good as skinny feels." No more big bum for me!

vocabulary.entry: bum [n.] /bʌm/ 屁股 (口语词汇；英式英语)

vocabulary.example: She splashed out on a pair of designer jeans.

vocabulary.example: She decided to go on a diet after the Christmas holidays.
vocabulary.translation: 圣诞节假期后她决定节食。

vocabulary.entry: calories [n. pl.] /ˈkæləriz/ 卡路里 (单数: calorie)
vocabulary.example: You need to burn off the calories you consume through exercise.
vocabulary.translation: 你需要通过运动消耗掉摄入的卡路里。

vocabulary.entry: cook from scratch [phr.] /kʊk frɒm skrætʃ/ 从头开始做饭 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: I prefer to cook from scratch using fresh ingredients.
vocabulary.translation: 我更喜欢用新鲜食材从头开始做饭。

vocabulary.entry: obesity [n.] /əʊˈbɪsɪti/ 肥胖 (专业词汇；医学)
vocabulary.example: Obesity is a major risk factor for heart disease.
vocabulary.translation: 肥胖是心脏病的主要风险因素。

vocabulary.entry: weight loss [n.] /weɪt lɒs/ 减肥 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: A balanced diet is essential for healthy weight loss.
vocabulary.translation: 均衡饮食对健康减肥至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: food labels [n. pl.] /fuːd ˈleɪbəlz/ 食品标签 (单数: food label)
vocabulary.example: Always check food labels for sugar and salt content.
vocabulary.translation: 务必查看食品标签上的糖和盐含量。

vocabulary.example: He has been trying to reduce his waistline by exercising more.
vocabulary.translation: 他一直想通过多运动来减小腰围。

vocabulary.entry: overeating [n.] /ˌəʊvərˈiːtɪŋ/ 暴饮暴食；吃得过多
vocabulary.example: Overeating is a common cause of weight gain.
vocabulary.translation: 吃得过多是体重增加的常见原因。

vocabulary.entry: plate size [n.] /pleɪt saɪz/ 盘子大小 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: Reducing your plate size can help you eat less.
vocabulary.translation: 减小盘子尺寸可以帮助你少吃东西。

vocabulary.entry: calories served [n. pl.] /ˈkælərɪz sɜːvd/ 提供的卡路里 (单数: calorie served)
vocabulary.example: Smaller portions mean fewer calories served.
vocabulary.translation: 较小的份量意味着提供的卡路里更少。

vocabulary.entry: tricking themselves [phr.] /ˈtrɪkɪŋ ðəmˈselvz/ 欺骗自己 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: By using smaller plates, you're not really tricking yourself into eating less.
vocabulary.translation: 用小盘子并没有真正欺骗自己少吃东西。

vocabulary.entry: seconds and thirds [n. pl.] /ˈsekəndz ənd θɜːdz/ 第二份和第三份 (固定搭配；口语)
vocabulary.example: The food was so good that everyone went back for seconds and thirds.
vocabulary.translation: 食物太好吃了，每个人都回去盛了第二份和第三份。

vocabulary.entry: inspiring image [n.] /ɪnˈspaɪərɪŋ ˈɪmɪdʒ/ 鼓舞人心的图片
vocabulary.example: An inspiring image on your fridge can motivate you to eat healthily.
vocabulary.translation: 冰箱上鼓舞人心的图片可以激励你健康饮食。

vocabulary.entry: wise quote [n.] /waɪz kwəʊt/ 明智的引语
vocabulary.example: She began her speech with a wise quote from Confucius.
vocabulary.translation: 她以孔子的一句明智引语开始了演讲。

vocabulary.example: She dreamed of becoming a supermodel and walking the runways of Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 她梦想成为超模，走在巴黎的T台上。

vocabulary.entry: skinny [adj.] /ˈskɪni/ 苗条的 (口语词汇；常带主观色彩)
vocabulary.example: She's much too skinny to be a healthy weight.

sentences.english: As supermodel Kate Moss once said: "Nothing tastes as good as skinny feels."
sentences.chinese: 正如超模凯特·莫斯曾经说过的：“没有什么比苗条的感觉更好。”

sentences.english: No more big bum for me!
